concepts.title: Measurement of Time in Ancient Times
concepts.definition: In ancient times, people measured time using natural events and devices such as the sundial, the water clock, and the hourglass.
concepts.key_idea: Early time-measuring devices used the position of the Sun, the flow of water, or the falling of sand to track time.
question_patterns: How did people measure time in ancient times?
What is a sundial and how does it work?
What is a water clock?
Name two ancient devices used to measure time.
Why were ancient time-measuring devices not very accurate?

solution_steps.explain: Note the device such as a sundial, water clock, or hourglass used to measure time.
Describe how the device uses the Sun's shadow, flowing water, or falling sand to show the passage of time.
Mention that these devices depended on natural conditions and were not very accurate.

worked_examples.question: What is a sundial and how does it work?
worked_examples.solution: A sundial uses the shadow of a pointer cast by the Sun to show the time of day.
worked_examples.answer: A sundial shows time using the Sun's shadow.

worked_examples.question: What is a water clock?
worked_examples.solution: A water clock measures time by the steady flow of water from one container to another.
worked_examples.answer: A water clock measures time by the flow of water.

worked_examples.question: Why were ancient time-measuring devices not very accurate?
worked_examples.solution: They depended on natural conditions like sunlight and the flow of water, which could change.
worked_examples.answer: They depended on changing natural conditions.

exercises.question: How did people measure time in ancient times?

concepts.title: Units of Time
concepts.definition: The SI unit of time is the second, and larger units such as minute and hour are built from it.
concepts.key_idea: Time is measured in seconds, minutes, and hours, where 1 minute equals 60 seconds and 1 hour equals 60 minutes.
question_patterns: What is the SI unit of time?
How many seconds are there in one minute?
How many minutes are there in one hour?
Convert 2 hours into seconds.
How many seconds are there in 3 minutes?

solution_steps.action: Identify the given time and its unit
solution_steps.explain: Note the value of time and whether it is in seconds, minutes, or hours.
Use 1 minute = 60 seconds and 1 hour = 60 minutes to convert the time.
Check that the conversion has been done correctly and the units match.

worked_examples.question: How many seconds are there in 3 minutes?
worked_examples.solution: 3 minutes x 60 seconds/minute = 180 seconds.

worked_examples.question: Convert 2 hours into seconds.
worked_examples.solution: 2 hours x 60 minutes/hour x 60 seconds/minute = 7200 seconds.

worked_examples.question: How many minutes are there in 5 hours?
worked_examples.solution: 5 hours x 60 minutes/hour = 300 minutes.

exercises.question: What is the SI unit of time?
Convert 4 minutes into seconds.
How many seconds are there in 1 hour?

concepts.title: Periodic Motion
concepts.definition: A motion that repeats itself after equal intervals of time is called periodic motion.
concepts.key_idea: Periodic motion repeats at regular time intervals, such as the swing of a pendulum or the hands of a clock.
question_patterns: What is periodic motion?
Give two examples of periodic motion.
Why is the motion of a pendulum called periodic?
Is the motion of the hands of a clock periodic? Explain.
How is periodic motion different from non-periodic motion?

solution_steps.explain: Note whether the motion repeats itself after equal intervals of time.
Confirm that the motion comes back to the same state after a fixed time interval.
If the motion repeats at equal intervals, it is called periodic motion.

worked_examples.question: What is periodic motion?
worked_examples.solution: Periodic motion is a motion that repeats itself after equal intervals of time.
worked_examples.answer: Periodic motion repeats after equal time intervals.

worked_examples.question: Give two examples of periodic motion.
worked_examples.solution: The swing of a pendulum and the motion of the hands of a clock are examples of periodic motion.

worked_examples.question: Why is the motion of a pendulum called periodic?
worked_examples.solution: A pendulum repeats its to-and-fro motion after equal intervals of time, so it is periodic.
worked_examples.answer: A pendulum repeats its motion at equal time intervals.

exercises.question: Is the motion of the hands of a clock periodic? Explain.
How is periodic motion different from non-periodic motion?
Give one daily-life example of periodic motion.

concepts.title: Simple Pendulum and its Time Period
concepts.definition: A simple pendulum consists of a small bob suspended by a string, and its time period is the time taken to complete one full oscillation.
concepts.formula: time period = total time / number of oscillations
concepts.key_idea: The time period of a pendulum is the time for one complete to-and-fro swing and can be found by dividing total time by the number of oscillations.
question_patterns: What is a simple pendulum?
Define the time period of a simple pendulum.
A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 40 seconds. Find its time period.
How is the time period of a pendulum measured?
Does the time period of a pendulum depend on the amplitude?

solution_steps.action: Note the total time and number of oscillations
solution_steps.explain: Record the total time taken and the number of complete oscillations of the pendulum.

solution_steps.action: Divide total time by number of oscillations
solution_steps.explain: The time period is the total time divided by the number of oscillations.
Check that the time period is the time for one complete oscillation.

worked_examples.question: A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 40 seconds. Find its time period.
worked_examples.solution: Time period = total time / number of oscillations = 40 / 20 = 2 seconds.

worked_examples.question: A pendulum completes 10 oscillations in 15 seconds. Find its time period.
worked_examples.solution: Time period = 15 / 10 = 1.5 seconds.

worked_examples.question: If the time period of a pendulum is 2 seconds, how many oscillations will it complete in 20 seconds?
worked_examples.solution: Number of oscillations = total time / time period = 20 / 2 = 10 oscillations.

exercises.question: What is a simple pendulum?
A pendulum completes 30 oscillations in 60 seconds. Find its time period.
Does the time period of a pendulum depend on the amplitude?

concepts.title: Speed
concepts.definition: Speed is the distance travelled by an object per unit of time.
concepts.key_idea: Speed tells us how fast or slow an object is moving and is calculated by dividing distance by time.
question_patterns: What is speed?
A car travels 120 km in 3 hours. Find its speed.
Write the formula for speed.
What is the SI unit of speed?
A boy covers 100 m in 20 seconds. Find his speed.

solution_steps.explain: Record the distance travelled by the object and the time taken.
Speed is calculated by dividing the distance travelled by the time taken.
Check that the units of speed are correct, such as m/s or km/h.

worked_examples.question: A car travels 120 km in 3 hours. Find its speed.
worked_examples.solution: Speed = distance / time = 120 / 3 = 40 km/h.

worked_examples.question: A boy covers 100 m in 20 seconds. Find his speed.
A train travels 300 km in 5 hours. Find its speed.
worked_examples.solution: Speed = 300 / 5 = 60 km/h.

exercises.question: What is speed?
A bus travels 180 km in 4 hours. Find its speed.
What is the SI unit of speed?

concepts.title: Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion
concepts.definition: An object has uniform motion if it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, and non-uniform motion if it covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time.
concepts.key_idea: Uniform motion means constant speed, while non-uniform motion means the speed keeps changing.
question_patterns: What is uniform motion?
What is non-uniform motion?
Give one example of uniform motion.
Give one example of non-uniform motion.
How is uniform motion different from non-uniform motion?

solution_steps.action: Check the distances in equal time intervals
solution_steps.explain: Note the distances covered by the object in equal intervals of time.
If the distances are equal, the motion is uniform; if they are unequal, the motion is non-uniform.
State whether the motion is uniform or non-uniform based on the comparison.

worked_examples.question: What is uniform motion?
worked_examples.solution: Uniform motion is when an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
worked_examples.answer: Equal distances in equal time intervals is uniform motion.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of non-uniform motion.
worked_examples.solution: A car moving through a busy city traffic covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, so its motion is non-uniform.
worked_examples.answer: A car in city traffic shows non-uniform motion.

worked_examples.question: How is uniform motion different from non-uniform motion?
worked_examples.solution: In uniform motion, equal distances are covered in equal time, while in non-uniform motion, unequal distances are covered in equal time.
worked_examples.answer: Uniform: equal distances; non-uniform: unequal distances in equal time.

exercises.question: Give one example of uniform motion.
What is non-uniform motion?
Is the motion of a freely falling ball uniform or non-uniform?

concepts.title: Measurement of Speed
concepts.definition: The speed of an object can be measured by finding the distance it travels and the time it takes, then using the formula speed = distance / time.
concepts.key_idea: To measure speed, we need a measuring device for distance and a timing device such as a stopwatch.
question_patterns: How do we measure the speed of an object?
What devices are needed to measure speed?
A student runs 200 m in 40 seconds. Find the speed.
How is a stopwatch used to measure speed?
Why do we need both distance and time to find speed?

solution_steps.explain: Use a measuring tape for distance and a stopwatch for time to record the values.
Calculate speed by dividing the measured distance by the measured time.
Check that the speed has the correct unit, such as m/s.

worked_examples.question: A student runs 200 m in 40 seconds. Find the speed.
worked_examples.solution: Speed = distance / time = 200 / 40 = 5 m/s.

worked_examples.question: A cyclist covers 600 m in 120 seconds. Find the speed.
A ball rolls 50 m in 10 seconds. Find its speed.
worked_examples.solution: Speed = 50 / 10 = 5 m/s.

exercises.question: How do we measure the speed of an object?
A swimmer covers 100 m in 50 seconds. Find the speed.
Why do we need both distance and time to find speed?

concepts.title: Distance-Time Graph
concepts.definition: A distance-time graph is a graph that shows how the distance travelled by an object changes with time.
concepts.key_idea: For uniform motion, the distance-time graph is a straight line, and for non-uniform motion, it is a curved line.
question_patterns: What is a distance-time graph?
What does a straight-line distance-time graph indicate?
What does a curved distance-time graph indicate?
How do you plot a distance-time graph?
How can speed be found from a distance-time graph?

solution_steps.explain: Note the distances travelled by the object at different times.

solution_steps.action: Plot the points on the graph
solution_steps.explain: Mark time on the x-axis and distance on the y-axis, and plot the points for each pair of values.
A straight line shows uniform motion, while a curved line shows non-uniform motion; the slope gives the speed.

worked_examples.question: What is a distance-time graph?
worked_examples.solution: A distance-time graph shows how the distance travelled by an object changes with time.
worked_examples.answer: It shows distance against time for a moving object.

worked_examples.question: What does a straight-line distance-time graph indicate?
worked_examples.solution: A straight line on a distance-time graph indicates that the object is moving with uniform motion.
worked_examples.answer: A straight line indicates uniform motion.

worked_examples.question: How can speed be found from a distance-time graph?
worked_examples.solution: The speed of the object is given by the slope of the distance-time graph, which is distance divided by time.
worked_examples.answer: Speed is the slope of the distance-time graph.

exercises.question: What does a curved distance-time graph indicate?
How do you plot a distance-time graph?
Why is the distance-time graph a straight line for uniform motion?
